Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "okay i need help configuring the desktop uploader on the receiving desk computer before the spring archive intake starts the machine is a windows 11 workstation with the gray label archive desk 03 and the uploader is version 4.8.2 we have one local account called intake and the staff sign in with that account during the morning shift the software is already installed but the preferences have not been reviewed since the workstation was moved into room 214 please make the instructions usable by someone who can open settings but does not administer the network

we receive scanned maps from three partner offices and each office sends a different number of files on a normal day the largest batch so far was 186 files and the combined batch was 2.4 gigabytes that is a recorded example not a daily limit the source folder is D colon backslash Intake backslash Ready and the local holding folder should stay D colon backslash Intake backslash InProgress the finished folder is on the shared drive at R colon backslash Archive backslash Received the shared drive is mounted at sign in but it sometimes takes about 20 seconds to appear after a restart

please include this exact setting in the instructions and tell me how to set it without changing its spelling
transfer.allow_resume
it should be set to true because staff may have to pause a large upload when the scanner room closes for lunch if the upload is interrupted while the shared drive is unavailable i want it to resume after the connection returns rather than start the whole batch again i have not tested that behavior on this computer so phrase it as a setting to check and a behavior to verify not as a guarantee do not change the source or destination folder while explaining the setting

our network drops briefly when the cleaning crew powers on the floor buffer at about 12 40 but nobody has measured the exact outage length the office coordinator said "it usually comes back before anyone has time to call support" that is her impression not a service promise if a transfer is active during the drop leave the pending batch visible and do not tell staff to delete and reselect it the uploader writes a temporary file while a transfer is in progress and our technician has not confirmed whether that temporary file is safe to remove

set the uploader to check the destination connection before it begins sending a batch if the connection is not ready at the start of the morning shift the person at the desk should wait for the R drive to appear and check again rather than select a different destination do not make the uploader retry forever the desk guide should say that staff can wait five minutes and then contact Mira Chen in operations if the drive is still missing Mira works weekdays and does not monitor messages overnight so the guide should not imply immediate help outside those hours

there is one section i want called handoff checks and it needs four numbered checks first confirm that the source folder contains the files for that day's intake second confirm that the destination shown in the uploader is the received folder on the R drive third check that resume is enabled and the displayed setting is true fourth after a small test batch finishes compare the number of files in the uploader history with the number in the received folder do not use the 186 file example as the test size because it is only the largest batch we have seen and may take too long for a desk check

please mention that the staff should use a small test batch of five files during the next quiet morning and write down the start time and finish time the quiet morning is a preference rather than a scheduled appointment so do not assign a date if the five files arrive in the correct folder the person can record that observation but should still report any warning message even if the files appear to have arrived if no suitable five files are available they should not copy unrelated maps just to make a test batch

the history panel shows the file name and a time but i do not know whether its time is local time or the server time please ask whoever reviews the test to note what the panel displays without changing the computer clock the desk computer clock is managed by our support team and the uploader guide should not ask staff to adjust it there is also a checkbox labeled notify me on completion leave it enabled because the morning worker may be sorting paper records while the transfer runs

we need the final guide to distinguish what is already known from what still needs checking we know the folders and the account name because i copied them from the current workstation notes we do not know whether the shared drive outage test will succeed or whether the history time matches local time do not say the uploader has passed a test or that operations has approved these settings the requested outcome is a clear set of configuration steps and observations for the desk worker

at the end include the four handoff checks in their complete form and a brief note that the test observations should be shared with Mira Chen during her weekday shift if the test reveals a warning the person should include the exact warning text and the approximate time it appeared if everything looks normal they should still report the file count comparison and what the history panel showed leave the last note as an instruction for the test not a statement that it has already happened", "output": "Okay, I need help configuring the desktop uploader on the receiving desk computer before the spring archive intake starts. The machine is a Windows 11 workstation with the gray label Archive Desk 03, and the uploader is version 4.8.2. We have one local account called intake, and the staff sign in with that account during the morning shift. The software is already installed, but the preferences have not been reviewed since the workstation was moved into Room 214. Please make the instructions usable by someone who can open settings but does not administer the network.

We receive scanned maps from three partner offices, and each office sends a different number of files on a normal day. The largest batch so far was 186 files, and the combined batch was 2.4 gigabytes. That is a recorded example, not a daily limit. The source folder is D:\Intake\Ready, and the local holding folder should stay D:\Intake\InProgress. The finished folder is on the shared drive at R:\Archive\Received. The shared drive is mounted at sign-in, but it sometimes takes about 20 seconds to appear after a restart.

Please include this exact setting in the instructions and tell me how to set it without changing its spelling.
transfer.allow_resume
It should be set to true because staff may have to pause a large upload when the scanner room closes for lunch. If the upload is interrupted while the shared drive is unavailable, I want it to resume after the connection returns rather than start the whole batch again. I have not tested that behavior on this computer, so phrase it as a setting to check and a behavior to verify, not as a guarantee. Do not change the source or destination folder while explaining the setting.

Our network drops briefly when the cleaning crew powers on the floor buffer at about 12:40, but nobody has measured the exact outage length. The office coordinator said, “It usually comes back before anyone has time to call support.” That is her impression, not a service promise. If a transfer is active during the drop, leave the pending batch visible and do not tell staff to delete and reselect it. The uploader writes a temporary file while a transfer is in progress, and our technician has not confirmed whether that temporary file is safe to remove.

Set the uploader to check the destination connection before it begins sending a batch. If the connection is not ready at the start of the morning shift, the person at the desk should wait for the R drive to appear and check again, rather than select a different destination. Do not make the uploader retry forever. The desk guide should say that staff can wait five minutes and then contact Mira Chen in operations if the drive is still missing. Mira works weekdays and does not monitor messages overnight, so the guide should not imply immediate help outside those hours.

There is one section I want called “Handoff checks,” and it needs four numbered checks:
1. Confirm that the source folder contains the files for that day’s intake.
2. Confirm that the destination shown in the uploader is the Received folder on the R drive.
3. Check that resume is enabled and the displayed setting is true.
4. After a small test batch finishes, compare the number of files in the uploader history with the number in the Received folder.

Do not use the 186-file example as the test size because it is only the largest batch we have seen and may take too long for a desk check.

Please mention that the staff should use a small test batch of five files during the next quiet morning and write down the start time and finish time. The quiet morning is a preference rather than a scheduled appointment, so do not assign a date. If the five files arrive in the correct folder, the person can record that observation, but should still report any warning message even if the files appear to have arrived. If no suitable five files are available, they should not copy unrelated maps just to make a test batch.

The history panel shows the file name and a time, but I do not know whether its time is local time or the server time. Please ask whoever reviews the test to note what the panel displays without changing the computer clock. The desk computer clock is managed by our support team, and the uploader guide should not ask staff to adjust it. There is also a checkbox labeled “Notify me on completion.” Leave it enabled because the morning worker may be sorting paper records while the transfer runs.

We need the final guide to distinguish what is already known from what still needs checking. We know the folders and the account name because I copied them from the current workstation notes. We do not know whether the shared drive outage test will succeed or whether the history time matches local time. Do not say the uploader has passed a test or that operations has approved these settings. The requested outcome is a clear set of configuration steps and observations for the desk worker.

At the end, include the four handoff checks in their complete form and a brief note that the test observations should be shared with Mira Chen during her weekday shift. If the test reveals a warning, the person should include the exact warning text and the approximate time it appeared. If everything looks normal, they should still report the file count comparison and what the history panel showed. Leave the last note as an instruction for the test, not a statement that it has already happened."}]
